_comment: # pragma: stub — hand-labelled recall@k probes for #329. Starter set of 10; the 30-pair target is a follow-up. One JSON object per line. anchor_excerpt is the text the API receives; ground_truth_event_date points at the historical statement that should top retrieval. ground_truth_axes is the axis or axes that justified the match. notes is free-text for the reviewer.

anchor_excerpt: The Committee will employ all available tools to promote economic recovery and price stability and intends to keep the target range for the federal funds rate at the current exceptionally low level.
notes: Crisis-era dovish-easing; same stance + same factor (unconventional accommodation)

anchor_excerpt: The Committee judges that economic conditions warrant a gradual removal of policy accommodation as the labor market continues to strengthen.
Inflation remains elevated, reflecting supply and demand imbalances. The Committee anticipates ongoing increases in the target range.
notes: Hawkish-inflation pair; all three axes overlap

anchor_excerpt: The coronavirus outbreak has harmed communities and disrupted economic activity. The Committee expects to maintain this target range until it is confident that the economy has weathered recent events.
notes: Pandemic emergency-easing; topic = pandemic, stance = dovish

anchor_excerpt: The Committee judges that some further gradual increases in the target range will be consistent with sustained expansion of economic activity.
In light of the implications of global developments for the economic outlook, the Committee decided to lower the target range for the federal funds rate.
If incoming information broadly supports the Committee's expectation, the Committee currently anticipates that it would be appropriate to moderate the monthly pace of purchases.
Recent developments are likely to result in tighter credit conditions for households and businesses and to weigh on economic activity, hiring, and inflation.
The Committee currently anticipates that economic conditions are likely to warrant exceptionally low levels for the federal funds rate at least through mid-2013.
The Committee expects that economic conditions will evolve in a manner that will warrant gradual increases in the federal funds rate.
